page0.text:
I shop at the tofu shop first thing in the morning under the clear blue sky.
I buy three blocks of silken tofu with the three hundred yen that was on the table.
"Oh, how commendable of you to come on a Sunday, Shirou!"
I go home drinking the soy milk that the second-generation tofu shop owner had given me for free.

page1.text:
"...Yeah, I'm content."
This is perfect.
It is a morning that feels good with nothing to complain about situation-wise.

page2.text:
"...But, I feel like I got ripped off..."
I tilt my head in wonder and look up at the sky.
A big serving of tofu and a sixty yen soy milk.
I don't think you can easily find things that can compare to this happiness.

page3.text:
I take my time to walk back home and ponder how to use the tofu for twenty minutes.
Before I realized it, it was 8:30 AM.

page4.text: "Good morning, Shirou. You are at ease this morning."

page5.text:
"Mm? Oh, morning, Saber. I can relax since it's Sunday and there's no school today. My body feels good too, so let's go to the dojo after breakfast."
"Yes, that would be great. So your numbness has healed?"

page6.text:
"Oh, come to think of it, yeah.
I was able to walk comfortably from the shopping district, so it seems mostly healed... Well, it's still slightly heavy, but it should be fully healed by tomorrow."

page7.text: "That is good. I have no place if my Master is still wounded. It makes me relieved to see you standing in the kitchen as usual."

page8.text:
Saber takes a seat at her usual position beside the table.
I have to say that Fuji-nee and Tohsaka are sleepyheads for not waking up yet, but it's a weekend, so I should let them sleep until breakfast is ready.

page9.text:
"Good morning, Rin. It seems you were able to sleep well last night."
...Oh.
It looks like Tohsaka woke up while we were talking.

page10.text:
"...Morning. Not really. The sunlight was bright, and there were some people moving about even past midnight."
Tohsaka replies to Saber while entering the living room.

page11.text:
Well.
I don't want to complain first thing in the morning, but I need to at least find out why she took all the bread.

page12.text:
"Morning, Tohsaka. This is straight to the point, but about this morning..."
My breath stops.
Tohsaka's wearing unfamiliar clothes again first thing in the morning.

page13.text:
"Oof..."
My heartbeat rapidly increases.
...It's because of those bright red clothes.
It hurts my eyes so much that I completely forgot what I wanted to say.

page14.text:
"...I'm making breakfast. Have some tea while you're waiting."
I keep my calm and place two teacups on the table.
However...

page15.text:
"Why are you taking your time? We're going out today, so hurry up and get ready."
Tohsaka glares at me, as if to say that breakfast can come later.

page16.text:
"Huh...? Um, where are we going?"
"To the neighboring town. Actually, I want to go further, but we don't have the leisure, right? So it's a compromise."

page17.text:
"...?"
Is this some sort of pre-emptive strike?
I can't seem to grasp Tohsaka's intentions.

page18.text:
"Okay. I get that it's a compromise, but for what?"
"We're going to go have fun, of course. It's a date."

page19.text:
"A date... Who and who?"
"You and I."
She says clearly.
"...?"
After I tilt my head in wonder...

page20.text:
"D-DATE... ME AND TOHSAKAAAAAAA!?"
"Who else is there? I told you last night."
...
Hold on.
What? This is so sudden. My mind can't process everything that's happening!

page21.text:
"Come on, let's go. I figured this would happen, so I made lunch. Here, hold this and follow me."
Tohsaka pushes the green tote bag onto me and leaves the living room.
